translations.answer: The contributors first suggested verifying the orientation convention on both sides; the original author then confirmed a minor calculation error from quaternions to Euler ZYX, which was corrected, allowing quadrupedal locomotion. Threads simultaneously warned that MPC had additional strong feedback on base pose/twist when using measured-state feedback, but the original author did not verify 'only tracking desired base acceleration' and thus it can only be considered as a subsequent troubleshooting item.
translations.applicability: Applies to the interface between OCS2 MPC, RaiSim, and self-developed WBC for floating base pose transmission; specific state layouts, rotation order, and units must be verified against the target code.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record on environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author tried at 1 kHz and 1 Hz, and other MRT/MPC/observation frequencies without direct success.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author corrected the quaternions-to-Euler ZYX calculation, allowing quadrupedal locomotion.
translations.details.attempts.2: The author fed full state and input feedback to MPC, and only tracked base pose and leg joint angles in WBC initial testing; low-pass filtering of real observation feedback was applied.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Verify the orientation convention and quaternions-to-Euler ZYX conversion between MPC and simulation/WBC on both sides.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Separate MPC feedforward from WBC's additional base pose/twist feedback, and check if the MPC's existing feedback is repeated.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Do not rely solely on changing observation update frequency to determine the root cause; also check the continuity of reference states and input coordinates.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Correcting the quaternions-to-Euler ZYX conversion is the original author's confirmed valid fix.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Low-pass filtering of observation feedback in the author's current walking test made MPC reference smoother and more stable, but this is an engineering practice for that environment only.
translations.details.environments.0: ANYmal C, RaiSim, self-developed WBC 1 kHz, mrtDesiredFrequency 1 kHz, mpcDesiredFrequency=-1 (author's machine approx 250 Hz); no OCS2 commit provided.
translations.details.limits.0: The post does not publicize the orientation conversion code, filter type, cutoff frequency, or delay, so it cannot replicate a general filter parameter.
translations.details.limits.1: The contributor suggests only tracking MPC desired base acceleration, but the original author only stated it would be attempted, and the thread did not provide a retest result.
translations.details.limits.2: The low-pass filter result only covers the author's current walking test and does not cover more dynamic motion.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author confirmed quadrupedal locomotion after correcting the orientation conversion.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The original author reported a stable WBC after low-pass filtering, and the contributor acknowledges the current result, while warning of phase delay risks in dynamic actions.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the RaiSim measurement state is fed back to OCS2 MPC, the quadruped does not walk, drifts, or jumps, what should be verified first?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Can low-pass filtering of MPC observation feedback be used as a general stabilizing scheme?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Offline validation of orientation convention, units, and symbols is required before real-world integration; any new filters must measure phase delay and be gradually closed in low-speed/suspended or safe support conditions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original author ultimately confirmed a minor calculation error in quaternions to Euler ZYX.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The contributor pointed out that additional base pose/twist error feedback in WBC could potentially overlap with MPC's own measurement state feedback, leading to closed-loop instability.
translations.details.symptoms.0: At 1 kHz observation update, the robot initially stands still, then drifts.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Reducing observation update to 1 Hz causes RViz robot position jumps and RaiSim side instability again.
translations.details.symptoms.2: The author tried multiple MRT/MPC/observation update frequencies without stabilization.
translations.media_summaries.0: First GIF has been verified at multiple times: left is RViz and RaiSim, left robot shows obvious multiple pose artifacts, right robot's pose is inconsistent with the left; no timestamps, numbers, or coordinates, so cannot quantify drift from the image.
translations.media_summaries.1: Second GIF has been verified at multiple times: left RViz robot's foot trajectory and pose and right RaiSim robot pose show significant jumps between frames; it supports the post's description of visual asynchrony/unsteadiness, but does not single out update frequency or orientation conversion as the root cause.
